opaque / opacity.definition: hard to see through or understand; opacity is the quality of being hard to understand

to be exposed to.definition: to be at risk of being affected by something, for example a loss

a single point of failure.definition: one part of a system whose failure stops or harms the whole system

in lockstep.definition: moving or changing together, exactly at the same time

to amplify / to dampen.definition: amplify = to make stronger or larger; dampen = to make weaker or smaller

a feedback loop.definition: a process in which a result feeds back into the cause and changes it again

a tipping point.definition: the moment when a small change makes a large and often irreversible change happen

a circuit breaker.definition: a rule or device that pauses a system, for example trading, when things move too fast

to rubber-stamp.definition: to approve something automatically without really checking it

to be on the hook for.definition: to be responsible, especially for paying for something

provided that / as long as / unless.definition: provided that and as long as introduce a condition that must be true; unless means 'if not'

to conflate X with Y.definition: to treat two different things as if they were the same

it stands to reason that.definition: it is logical or obvious that

what remains to be seen is whether.definition: we do not yet know whether; the answer is still open

with the caveat that.definition: adding a warning or condition to what you just said

that’s a big if.definition: the condition is very uncertain, so the conclusion is doubtful

to cut both ways.definition: to have both good and bad effects, or to support both sides of an argument

to read too much into something.definition: to find more meaning in something than is really there

Reporting verbs.definition: choose the verb by how strongly the speaker committed: asserts = states as true; imagines = pictures a scenario; asks = poses a question; warns = cautions

Three layers.definition: separate what was said, what the evidence shows, and your own interpretation

Hedging ladder.definition: verbs ordered from strong to weak commitment: shows, suggests, is consistent with, hints at

Concession, then your point.definition: admit a point with 'Granted' or 'While it is true that', then give your own point with 'But'

if-clause without will.definition: after if, use the present tense for a future condition

evidence (uncountable).definition: evidence, information and advice have no plural; count them with 'a piece of'

general nouns, no article.definition: abstract or general nouns take no article in general statements; use 'the' for something specific
general nouns, no article.right: Finance is complicated. / The financial system is complicated.
